artifacts.summary: 8-phase plan making the /orchestrate blocked classifier row discriminating via state.json dependency lookup, with full co-maintenance propagation across 7 source-store files.

memory_candidates.content: Layered orchestration pipelines can lose a signal rather than lack a gate: an upstream admission gate correctly computes an ordering constraint (dependency-graph eligibility), then a downstream triage classifier re-derives its verdict purely from a stale literal status string and unconditionally discards that computation. The symptom is an infinite non-converging skip loop, not a hard failure, because nothing ever rewrites the stale status. Two design lessons generalize: (1) when the classifier already slurps the full state file, the fix is a second lookup against data already in memory -- not a new CLI argument, call-site change, or I/O class; (2) 'is the blocker among my sibling candidates?' is the tempting-but-wrong discriminator, because a just-terminated predecessor has already been dropped from the shrinking per-cycle eligible set and is absent from the candidate list in exactly the cycle the fix must handle. Look up the dependency's own status in the shared state instead. Corollary: an empty dependency list must be its own explicit non-discharging branch, since 'all elements satisfy P' is vacuously true over an empty list.
